doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sideman work and Charlie Singleton's background dates
summary: He played in many bands and did background recordings for singers with Charlie Singleton, learning a huge repertoire.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So who were you playing with? Were you the leader by this time?

Oh, no, I wasn’t the leader of a lot of the bands. I played with a lot of bands. A lot of bands. I played with a guy named Charlie Singleton. He made a lot of background records for singers, and I got that, too. That was a little extra money. It was great.
So no wonder you were learning all the tunes, had so many tunes in your bag.
I knew all the tunes. Knew all the music, all the tunes, and I was just assimilating them and cataloguing them.
So this is what you’re doing in 1950 and 1951... How long did you go to Darrow Institute?
I went there until I guess about ‘52.

‘52 happens to be the year that you start your long relationship with Blue Note Records and make your first sessions with Blue Note? But before we get there, I have just a couple of other questions. Did you ever play in any territory bands?
